lines.text: For thirty-one years, a cat named Biscuit kept the lighthouse burning.
Every night at dusk, she climbed the ninety-nine iron steps alone,
she trimmed the wick, she polished the great glass lens,
and she watched the fog roll in like a slow grey sea.
Then one October night, the supply boat never came.
The oil ran low, the wind rose, and a fishing boat was lost in the dark.
So Biscuit did the one thing no keeper had ever taught her.
She dragged the spare oil up, one small can at a time,
And at dawn, Biscuit finally slept, the lighthouse still burning.
